recipes.name: Jan's Pretzel Dogs
ingredients_raw: 1 (12 fluid ounce) can or bottle room temperature beer
0.25 cup kosher salt, divided - or to taste

steps.text: Heat beer in a saucepan over low heat until it reaches 110 degrees F (45 degrees C); pour into a bowl. Add sugar and 2 teaspoons kosher salt; sprinkle yeast on top and let stand for 5 minutes until yeast begins to foam.
Place bread flour and butter in a bread machine. Add yeast mixture; select Dough cycle.
Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C). Lightly grease 2 baking sheets or line with parchment paper. Beat egg yolk in a small bowl with 1 tablespoon water; set aside.
Stir baking soda into 10 cups water in a large pot until dissolved; bring to a boil.

Turn dough out onto a lightly-oiled surface; roll into a 10x20-inch rectangle. Slice dough into eighteen 1-inch wide strips; wrap each strip tightly around a hot dog in a spiral, pinching the edges to seal and leaving the ends open. About half an inch of hot dog should peek out of each end of the dough wrapper.
Drop 2 or 3 dough-wrapped hot dogs into the boiling water for 30 seconds.
Arrange boiled hot dogs on the prepared baking sheets. Brush each pretzel dog with egg yolk mixture; sprinkle with remaining 1/4 cup salt.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, about 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Jan's Pretzel Dogs
raw_recipe.description: Pretzel dogs made with homemade pretzel dough using beer, instead of water, for a richer flavor. Give this recipe a go at your next Super Bowl party!

video.description: Hot dogs wrapped in homemade pretzels make the perfect party snack.

review.reviewBody: UPDATE*** As the submitter of this recipe I would suggest to those of you worried about over browning bottoms, to use two cookie sheets together to bake on. My baking sheets are a heavy gauge metal and I also use a silpat on top of that so mine bake up just right. However, if you have a thin sheet, doubling up will help insulate the bottom and prevent over browning issues. Parchment paper will keep dough from sticking but I do suggest a good spray with PAM prior to use.*** These are easy and fun. My kid love 'em! We have made different kinds.... Turkey, beef, sausage, cheese....kids like the cheese dogs best! These never last long so I make a double batch and individually freeze the second batch for a special lunch treat! When I freeze for lunches I leave the salt off as it causes the bread to "sweat" while defrosting. The dough is also wonderful for regular pretzel or bite size pretzels. I highly recommend the recipe "Clone of a Pretzel Dip" from this site to accompany the pretzel bites!

-edit-
Thank you, Big "M"! My oven has a convection feature but I rarely think to use it. I went with your suggestion of convection, 400F, 11-12 minutes, plus I used a Silpat nonstick mat. The end result was a perfect balance of top and bottom browning. 

About the kosher salt -- I was surprised to read how widely the density can vary. Morton's Kosher is more than half again as dense as Diamond Crystal so the choice of salt in the dough would make a big difference. (I use Diamond Crystal for the dough but Morton's for the sprinkles.)

From past experience, I should also note that the quality of the hot dog matters a lot. We had tried different brands of cheese dogs and the brand makes a major difference.

I just made these for my family and they were delicious. Very easy to make. I don't have a bread machine so I copied what another viewer did and used my KA mixer, swapped out the paddle beater with the dough hook after the ingredients were mixed. I let the dough hook knead the dough for about 6 minutes. I used the Kirkland brand (long) hot dogs from Costco and cut each hot dog in half, and used half a strip of dough to wrap around each hot dog. Worked out perfect. I actually got 22 wrapped hot dogs. I love the fact that you can freeze them for later. Great recipe, will make again and again!! Thank you.

Great recipe. I halved it. I would add salt to the flour as it retards yeast growth. I used a stand mixer with a hook. Mixed yeast mixture, flour, and salt until dough came away from the bowl. Stopped for anout 10 minutes then continued until dough was smooth and elastic. Used a pizza cutter for the strips. Used smoked brats with jalapeno and cheese.

Great recipe! I doubled the sugar and used lil'smokies to turn these into an awesome appetizer. You need 2 regular packages if you want to use Lil'Smokies though. I also don't have a bread maker so I used my Kitchen Aid to knead for 8 minutes then let it rise for an hour on the proof setting in my over. No need for a second rise.

 Be careful with the flour though. I am experienced at bread making and didn't just dump it all together. I ended up with a whole cup of flour too much. Start with 3/4 of the recipe and add a little more at a time until the dough is soft and just a little sticky when you poke it with your finger.

My family loved this recipe and I will definitely make it again!

Wow wow wow. This was absolutely amazing! My husband and kids loved these and so did I! I studied breadmaking in a prestigious school but we've never tackled pretzels that used beer. And since my boys love hot dogs so much...I was desperate to make something That will be a complete snack for them when they're at school or work. Well this is it! So easy to make....I have a bread machine but did the kneading on my Kitchenaid mixer which was just fine....I think doing this by hand is ok as well as the dough is very forgiving. i let the dough rise for an hour then rolled the dough with a rolling pin then sliced in strips as indicated. Instead of the baking soda bath I used food grade lye used really for pretzels which gave my pretzels a lovely brown color in just 20 minutes of baking. Used sea salt for sprinkling. Thank you for sharing.

Im writing this review on behalf of my kids. They absolutely love these things! Easy to make and keeps them full! Great for a kids party! If Im going through all the trouble of making the dough, I chose to go to my local butcher and get fresh all beef links which I think makes a huge difference. Surprisingly different beers makes for a different taste. The last time I used Pyramid Hefeweizen and they were the best so far. This time around I turned them half way through the baking process and they browned evenly and perfectly.

This is a solid recipe. As is, it made 48 mini dogs. But it was more work than I think necessary. Second time making it, I spent $1.50 on premade pizza dough from deli and saved a lot of work. I cut in half regular dogs and used one package. Much easier and just as great. Next time I think I'll try cutting water/baking soda in half.

These were a big hit with my family! They were easy to make. I used water and regular unbleached flour. I used all the salt called for and sprinkled a few grains on top after brushing with the egg/water mixture. I used 10 regular hot dogs and 6 veggie dogs (Morning Star Farms). There were some left over scraps which I just tossed in the b.soda water, then baked. They were delicious, as well. I bake whole wheat bread/rolls/pizza almost every week, and out of all the bread dough I've made, this is the easiest I've ever worked with. I don't have a bread machine so did it by hand as always. I used 4 cups of flour plus what I put on the counter as I kneaded the dough. It was like playing with homemade Play Dough! It was such a nice texture. When wrapping the strip of dough around the hot dog, be sure to overlap the first end and pinch closed the last end so they stay together in the water. I made Cheese Dipping Sauce by Jackie Smith and that added a great taste. Thanks for the great recipe!

These were pretty good, I would make them again. My oven isn't true, so I baked them for the 15 minutes as directed, but they were a bit underdone inside (yet very brown). I added cheese and jalapeno on top like in the video, others with poppy seeds, and the rest with only kosher salt on top. Ironically, the ones with the kosher salt were the best. I also made a spicy ketchup and the dipping sauce mentioned by the submitter, "Clone of a Pretzel Dip". I found that dip to be too sweet overall. The next time I make this I plan to make a spicy cheese dipping sauce. I made 1/2 of the recipe which covered 1 package of hotdogs (10 count) nicely with 2 small balls (pretzel bites) leftover.

Wow my Hubby and his kids LOVED these! And so did I of course :p I DID NOT have a bread machine but I DO have a heavy duty mixer. I did the first 3 steps as directed except I had all the ingredients together in the bowl with the paddle attachment of my mixer until well incorporated. I replaced the paddle with the dough hook and set it on medium low speed for about 6 minutes to knead the dough. After that I covered the dough with plastic wrap and let it sit at room temp for about 1 hour and 15 minutes, until it doubled in size. I did everything else as instructed.
It is great! I use it for making just pretzels without the dogs...I did reduce the water and baking soda to just 4 cups water and 1/4 cup baking soda and that works just as well
Followed the recipe exactly except I used everything bagel instead of salt. Turned out great!

PERFECT! I made these in 2 batches, used single regular greased cookie sheets and they turned out seriously perfect! Not burned on bottoms, browned just right. So SO good. Will make regularly for sure!
Did this recipe change or am I losing it? I don’t remember there being beer in the recipe. I also don’t remember the instructions including a bread maker. I remember it being really good though.

First of all, one does not need a bread machine. One can make these by hand or use a stand mixer. Read the various comments on how people used differing methods with good results. Ours turned out just fine without the use of a bread making machine. We have done these manually. We let the dough rest over night--less kneading. We have done these with a stand mixer. The results didn't vary. Make sure you use parchment paper, a nonstick spray, or silicon mat to keep the pretzel bread from sticking. We check about three quarters of the time suggested due to oven variation.

Love this recipe. My husband and I use it all the time for pretzel dogs, but I also like to make homemade stromboli and the pretzel dough is so much easier to work with than pizza dough. And the flavor combination is amazing. My favorite is pepperoni and cheese, but I've done sausage, ham, spinach, and broccoli too. I have also made an all-cheese one with homemade ricotta, and dairy-free with vegan butter and cheese. I am told those are excellent as well. I have to experiment with how to get more filling inside without making the pretzel-bolis too large, though. Either they have too little filling, or they tear coming out of the water because they are too big.

Fantastic recipe, I didn't use a bread machine (following, I imagine, the line of many other reviewers), and found that 15 mins. was not enough in my oven so I added a few extra to fully cook the dough. Otherwise, absolutely delicious!

They were easy to make and my husband and I really enjoyed them. I cooked with 2 heavy cookie sheets and silicone baking mats. The bottoms weren't cooked after top was so I just turned them over and kept cooking until brown. Wonderful.
